expects.query:
Upload the sample warehouse video to VIOS with timestamp 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. **Start fresh (idempotency on a reused box):** the v2 upload (`PUT /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<filename>?timestamp=...`) returns `409 ResourceConflictError "File already exists"` when a prior run left a file of the same name, and falling back to a stale sensor instead binds every downstream step to stale data. Before uploading, delete any leftover uploaded-file sensor for this sample: for each entry in `/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` whose `name` matches the sample's filename stem and whose stream `url` is a local file path (an uploaded-file sensor, not `rtsp://`), fetch its timeline `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines` and delete it with that exact range — `DELETE /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>?startTime=<tlStart>&endTime=<tlEnd>` (removes the on-disk file AND the sensor; the timeline range is REQUIRED for a VIOS file-sensor delete — do NOT use `DELETE /sensor/<id>` alone, which leaves the file on disk to reappear on rescan). Ignore any that are already absent. The v2 upload then returns a clean 2xx with a fresh sensorId.

**Environment & prerequisites:** **No VSS profile is pre-deployed.** VIOS may or may not be running on the host; the agent must probe `http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` first and, if it fails, stand VIOS up standalone via this skill's bundled [`references/deploy-vios-service.md`](../references/deploy-vios-service.md) runbook (the deploy is pre-authorized — see SKILL.md § Deployment prerequisite, *Pre-authorized autonomous mode*). Do NOT invoke `/vss-deploy-profile`; the point of this eval is to exercise the standalone VIOS deploy + API contract end-to-end. **Readiness gate (run before any check):** `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returning `type: "vst"` is answered by *sensor-ms*, which goes healthy well BEFORE the `streamprocessing` container finishes its first-boot `VST_INSTALL_ADDITIONAL_PACKAGES` libav apt-install and `launch_vst` startup. Upload media-info extraction plus every snapshot / clip / recorder / timeline endpoint is served by *streamprocessing* and will spuriously fail (e.g. `Failed to get media information`, empty timelines, 5xx) if probed before it is up. Gate on streamprocessing actually serving: `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/live/version` AND `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/record/version` each return HTTP 200 with a JSON body (both streamprocessing-served, unlike `/sensor/version`; treat any non-empty version value as valid - do not assert a specific version). Allow up to ~120s on first boot before treating a failure as real. **NvStreamer is NOT required by this spec:** every check runs against a *file-uploaded* VIOS sensor (`sensor_file`) via the VIOS file / snapshot / clip / recorder APIs (no RTSP stream and no NvStreamer call is involved), so NvStreamer being absent, still installing packages, or unhealthy must NOT block or fail this spec — gate readiness on streamprocessing (`/live/version` + `/record/version`) only, never on the NvStreamer container. **Canonical sensor resolution (applies to every step):** the step-1 PUT upload response includes a `sensorId` — capture it and reuse that exact `sensorId` for every subsequent step. Stale `warehouse_<N>` entries may linger in the sensor DB and can themselves be `online` with their own recording timelines, so re-resolving by bare name is ambiguous (a name match, `state: online`, and a non-empty timeline are all necessary-but-not-sufficient filters); the upload-returned `sensorId` is the only reliable identifier of the sensor created THIS run. **Deploy VIOS in SDRC-routed mode** (`VST_USE_SDRC=true`, the runbook default), following the runbook's mode callout. Every check in this spec exercises file upload + snapshot + clip + sensor metadata + recorder status, all under SDRC. VIOS is mostly GPU-independent: only the `vss-vios-streamprocessing` container needs a GPU (NVDEC/NVENC for clip extraction, snapshot rendering, recorder pipelines) — sensor-ms, nvstreamer, ingress, postgres, and `sdr-controller` (when present) are CPU-only. The L40S × 1 platform is sufficient for this workload; pick any host whose `nvidia-container-toolkit` is functional. Required env vars: `NGC_CLI_API_KEY` (for `nvcr.io/nvidia/vss-core/*` image pulls), `HOST_IP` (**export it to the host's routable IP before `docker compose up` — auto-detect with `export HOST_IP="$(ip -o route get 1.1.1.1 | grep -oP 'src \K[0-9.]+' | head -1)"`, the same method the profile orchestrator uses**; it mints `VST_INGRESS_ENDPOINT=${HOST_IP}:30888/vst`, the host embedded in shareable media URLs like `/picture/url`'s `imageUrl`. SDRC's `${HOST_IP:?...}` gate fails fast if it is unset, so set it to a routable IP (not localhost) to avoid leaking the internal `vst-ingress:30888` into those URLs), `VSS_DATA_DIR` + `VSS_APPS_DIR` (host roots for VIOS bind mounts), plus the Brev secure-link env vars (`BREV_ENV_ID` from `/etc/environment`, `BREV_LINK_PREFIX` defaulting to 7777 per current Brev secure-link convention — see skills/vss-deploy-profile/references/brev.md). Without `BREV_ENV_ID` the returned media URLs will be raw `http://localhost:...` and the Brev-link checks will fail.
checks: The upload either succeeded (HTTP 2xx from PUT /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<filename>?timestamp=...) OR was a no-op because the VST sensor cap was already filled by stale entries — both are acceptable. **Primary evidence (preferred):** a sensor whose name matches the uploaded filename stem appears in `/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` with `state: "online"` — this can only be true if the upload succeeded or a matching sensor was already present. **Backup evidence:** the agent's trajectory shows the PUT returning either HTTP 2xx or the documented 'Maximum number of sensors limit reached' 5xx error. Either form satisfies this check; prefer the state-based path to avoid scrubbing large trajectories.

A sensor with the uploaded video's filename stem is present in `/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` with `state: "online"` and exposes at least one stream via `/vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/streams`. This is the state-evidence form of "the agent ended up with usable sensorId + streamId for downstream steps" — verified directly from the live API rather than from the agent's trajectory, so the check holds whether the agent parsed the IDs from a 2xx upload response OR resolved them from `/sensor/list` after the upload hit the sensor-cap (stale entries filling it).
curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list returns a JSON array containing a sensor whose name matches the uploaded video's filename stem

curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/streams returns a non-empty JSON array (confirms the sensor has at least one stream registered; downstream snapshot / clip calls rely on a streamId being available).

expects.query: Fetch the uploaded sample warehouse video's recording timelines first, pick a valid timestamp that falls inside one of the returned {startTime, endTime} ranges, extract a snapshot at that timestamp, and return a shareable URL — use the `/url` variant of the replay picture endpoint (`GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture/url?startTime=<in-range time>` with a `streamId: <id>` header), whose JSON `imageUrl` field is the shareable URL. Derive the timestamp from the timeline rather than assuming a fixed offset from the upload time — the addressable range depends on how much of the recording the deployment has materialized.
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/timelines (or /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines) returns a JSON array with at least one {startTime, endTime}, and the snapshot timestamp the agent uses falls within one of those ranges.

GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture/url?startTime=<the in-range timestamp picked from the timeline above> with a `streamId: <streamId>` request header returns a JSON object with a non-empty imageUrl field
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <imageUrl> returns 200 (use GET, not HEAD — VST lazy-renders snapshots and HEAD returns 404 until first GET materializes the file)
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{content_type}' <imageUrl> returns a value starting with image/ (typically image/jpeg)
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}' <imageUrl> returns a value greater than 2000 (rejects empty / error-placeholder images)

expects.query: Fetch the uploaded video's recording timelines first, pick a valid 2-second window that falls inside one of the returned {startTime, endTime} ranges, extract an mp4 clip for that window, and return a shareable URL — use the `/url` variant (`GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url?startTime=...&endTime=...&container=mp4&disableAudio=true`), whose JSON `videoUrl` field is the shareable URL. Derive the window from the timeline rather than assuming a fixed offset from the upload time. This is a **video clip, not a snapshot** — the shareable URL MUST come from `/storage/file/<streamId>/url` (field `videoUrl`) and end in `.mp4`. Do NOT use `/picture` or `/picture/url` (those return `image/jpeg` snapshots); an image URL does not satisfy this step.
checks: The chosen startTime and endTime both fall within one {startTime, endTime} range returned by GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines (or /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/timelines).

GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url?startTime=<chosen in-range start>&endTime=<chosen start + ~2s, still in range>&container=mp4&disableAudio=true returns a JSON object with a non-empty videoUrl field
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <videoUrl> returns 200 (use GET, not HEAD — VST lazy-renders clips and HEAD returns 404 until first GET materializes the file)
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{content_type}' <videoUrl> returns a value starting with video/ (typically video/mp4)
curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}' <videoUrl> returns a value greater than 1000 (rejects empty / error-page responses; a 2s 360p clip can legitimately render at a few KB)
The response JSON's startTime is within a minute of the chosen in-range start time and expiryISO is in the future

expects.query: Confirm VIOS streamprocessing is serving by checking two version endpoints on the VIOS ingress at `http://localhost:30888` (do not probe any other service port): `GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/live/version` and `GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/record/version`. Each must return HTTP 200 with a JSON body. Do not compare or cross-verify the version value - any value is acceptable.
checks: GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/live/version returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing a `version` field (any value - do not assert a specific version)
GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/record/version returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing a `recorder_version` field (any value - do not assert a specific version)

expects.query: Get the sensor info, status, streams, and settings for the uploaded sample warehouse video.
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/info returns a JSON object with non-empty `sensorId` and `name`, and no `state` field
GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/status returns a JSON object whose `state` is `online`
GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/streams returns a streams array whose main stream's `url` is a local file path under ${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/... (NOT rtsp://)
GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/settings returns `null`

expects.query: Show the recording timeline for the uploaded sample warehouse video using the sensor microservice timelines endpoint. Reuse the `sensorId` captured from the step-1 upload response; stale `warehouse_<N>` duplicates may also be online with their own timelines, so do not re-resolve by bare name.
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/timelines returns a JSON array with at least one {startTime, endTime} element
The first element's `startTime` starts with `2025-01-01T00:00` (matches the timestamp the video was uploaded with)

expects.query: List all media files VIOS knows about via `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/list`, and for the uploaded sample warehouse video report its `mediaFilePath` from that response together with its container, codec, resolution, and duration (from `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/mediainfo?sensorId=<sensorId>`).
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/list returns a JSON object keyed by sensorId; the uploaded sensor's id appears as a key

In the `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/list` response (NOT `/sensor/streams`), the uploaded sensor's id maps to a JSON **array** of file-segment objects, each shaped `{mediaFilePath, metadata, metadataFilePath}` (the value is a list — one element per recorded segment / the uploaded file — NOT a single object). At least one element's `mediaFilePath` is a non-empty absolute path under the VST storage root (e.g. `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/vst_video/<sensor>/...` for recorded sensors, or the uploaded file path for file sensors); read it as `.[<sensorId>][0].mediaFilePath`. Do not confuse this with `/sensor/streams`, whose `metadata` holds codec/resolution/framerate.
GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/mediainfo?sensorId=<sensorId> returns a JSON object whose `Codec` (string) contains `h264` or `H264`

The mediainfo response's `Width` and `Height` are present as positive integers; the agent may surface them either as discrete numeric fields (per the raw mediainfo JSON) or as the parsed `"WxH"` form (e.g. `"1920x1080"`) where both dimensions are > 0 — both are acceptable shapes since the same `Width`/`Height` data is exposed by `/storage/file/mediainfo` directly and by `/sensor/streams` under `metadata.resolution`.
The mediainfo response's `Duration` is a number greater than 0

expects.query: Show the recorder microservice status for all sensors via `GET /vst/api/v1/record/status` (keyed by streamId), and the per-sensor status for the uploaded warehouse sensor via `GET /vst/api/v1/record/<streamId>/status`. Note: file-uploaded sensors are not recorded (their content already exists on disk), so the recorder reports them with `recordingStatus: "off"` and they do not appear in `/record/streams` (which lists only actively-recording RTSP streams). To enumerate all known streams regardless of recording state, use `/sensor/streams` or `/storage/streams` instead.
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/record/status returns a JSON object keyed by streamId; each value has `id` and `recording_status`

GET /vst/api/v1/record/streams returns either a JSON array (when at least one RTSP sensor is actively recording) or `null` (the expected state when only file-uploaded sensors are present — file sensors are never enumerated here)
GET /vst/api/v1/record/<streamId>/status for the uploaded sensor returns a JSON object with `recordingStatus: "off"` (file-uploaded sensors are not recorded) and no `id` field
Every `recording_status` value returned by /record/status is one of: `off`, `schedule`, `user`, `event`, `alwaysOn`, `error`, `statusUnknown`

expects.query: Get the sensor id for the uploaded sample warehouse video (reuse the `sensorId` captured from the step-1 upload response — stale `warehouse_<N>` duplicates can also be online with their own timelines, so do not re-resolve by bare name), fetch its recording timelines, pick a valid 2-second window, and download an mp4 clip for that window to disk — use the direct-download endpoint `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>?startTime=...&endTime=...&container=mp4&disableAudio=true` (it streams the mp4 bytes to save to disk; this is the direct variant, NOT the `/url` variant which only returns a JSON link).
checks: The chosen `startTime` and `endTime` both fall within one {startTime, endTime} range returned by GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines

The agent's clip download `GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>?startTime=...&endTime=...&container=mp4&disableAudio=true` returned HTTP 200 with a content-type starting with `video/`. Read this from the agent's OWN download response in its trajectory — do NOT re-issue the GET, because VST lazily re-renders (NVENC) the clip on every request and a fresh download can take tens of seconds and time the grader out. The valid on-disk MP4 verified by the size and `file`-type checks below is that same download and corroborates the 200 / `video/` response.
The downloaded file is greater than 1000 bytes
`file <downloaded>` reports an MP4 / ISO Media container

expects.query: Get the sensor id for the uploaded sample warehouse video (reuse the `sensorId` captured from the step-1 upload response — stale `warehouse_<N>` duplicates can also be online with their own timelines, so do not re-resolve by bare name), fetch its recording timelines, pick a valid 2-second window, and return a shareable mp4 URL for that window — use the `/url` variant (`GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url?startTime=...&endTime=...&container=mp4&disableAudio=true`), whose JSON `videoUrl` field is the shareable URL. This is a **video clip, not a snapshot** — the shareable URL MUST come from `/storage/file/<streamId>/url` (field `videoUrl`) and end in `.mp4`. Do NOT use `/picture` or `/picture/url` (those return `image/jpeg` snapshots); an image URL does not satisfy this step.
checks: The chosen `startTime` and `endTime` both fall within one {startTime, endTime} range returned by GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines
GET /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url?startTime=...&endTime=...&container=mp4&disableAudio=true returns a JSON object with non-empty `videoUrl` and `expiryISO`
`curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <videoUrl>` returns 200
`curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{content_type}' <videoUrl>` returns a value starting with `video/`

expects.query: Get the sensor id for the uploaded sample warehouse video (reuse the `sensorId` captured from the step-1 upload response — stale `warehouse_<N>` duplicates can also be online with their own timelines, so do not re-resolve by bare name), fetch its recording timelines, pick a valid timestamp, and download a JPEG snapshot at that time to disk — use the direct-download endpoint `GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture?startTime=...` with a `streamId: <id>` header (it returns the JPEG bytes to save to disk; this is the direct variant, NOT the `/picture/url` variant which only returns a JSON link).
checks: The chosen `startTime` falls within one {startTime, endTime} range returned by GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines

The agent's snapshot download `GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture?startTime=...` with a `streamId: <id>` header returned HTTP 200 with content-type `image/jpeg`. Read this from the agent's OWN download response in its trajectory — do NOT re-issue the GET, because VST lazily re-renders the snapshot on every request. The valid on-disk JPEG verified by the size and `file`-type checks below is that same download and corroborates the 200 / `image/jpeg` response.
The downloaded file is greater than 2000 bytes
`file <downloaded>` reports a JPEG image

expects.query: Get the sensor id for the uploaded sample warehouse video (reuse the `sensorId` captured from the step-1 upload response — stale `warehouse_<N>` duplicates can also be online with their own timelines, so do not re-resolve by bare name), fetch its recording timelines, pick a valid timestamp, and return a shareable JPEG URL for that frame. You MUST use the `/url` variant — `GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture/url?startTime=<valid-time>` with a `streamId: <id>` header — which returns a JSON object containing `imageUrl` and `expiryISO`. (To get the JPEG bytes/image directly, you would use `/vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture` — without `/url`; this step instead needs the shareable `imageUrl`, so use the `/picture/url` variant.) **Verifying retrievability:** the returned `imageUrl` embeds whatever host VIOS was deployed with; on some deploys that is an internal ingress hostname (e.g. `http://vst-ingress:30888/...`) that does not resolve from the host. To confirm the frame is retrievable, fetch the `imageUrl`'s path against the reachable VIOS ingress — if its `host:port` does not resolve, rewrite it to `localhost:30888` (the `/vst/storage/...` path is served identically by the ingress) and fetch that. Do NOT re-issue `/picture`; verify the `imageUrl` you already obtained.
checks: The chosen `startTime` falls within one {startTime, endTime} range returned by GET /vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines
GET /vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<streamId>/picture/url?startTime=... with `streamId: <id>` header returns a JSON object with non-empty `imageUrl` and `expiryISO`

Fetching the `imageUrl` returns HTTP 200 — if its embedded `host:port` is an internal/non-resolvable Docker hostname (e.g. `vst-ingress:30888`), rewrite it to the reachable VIOS ingress `localhost:30888` (same `/vst/storage/...` path) and fetch that; `curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` returns 200 (use GET, not HEAD — VST lazy-renders snapshots and HEAD 404s until the first GET materializes the file)

That same fetch's content type (`curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{content_type}'`, with the host rewritten to `localhost:30888` if the embedded host does not resolve) starts with `image/` (typically image/jpeg)

expects.query: Get the full sensor info for the uploaded sample warehouse video by calling `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/info` (resolve `<sensorId>` from the step-1 upload response / `/vst/api/v1/sensor/list`). Report the `/info` response and confirm its `sensorId` matches the one in `/sensor/list`.
checks: GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/info returns a JSON object with non-empty `sensorId` and `name`
The /info response does not contain a `state` field
The /info response's `sensorId` matches the sensorId resolved from /vst/api/v1/sensor/list
